item.title: [IGNITE-1361] MessagingExamplesSelfTest#testMessagingPingPongExample test fails.
item.description:

commit ee8504ec8669544fe0cefe822356967f27925c28
Author: ashutak <ashutak@gridgain.com>
Date: 2015-09-02T18:36:21Z

ignite-1361: PingPong example fixed

The root cause from logs:

Received message [msg=PING, sender=f039f3a9-c728-4714-8027-d5d9bb9b3621]
Received message [msg=PONG, sender=f039f3a9-c728-4714-8027-d5d9bb9b3621]
Received message [msg=PING, sender=f039f3a9-c728-4714-8027-d5d9bb9b3621]
Exception in thread "ignite-#8%pub-companion%" class org.apache.ignite.IgniteException: Received unexpected message: PING

The example send messages to wrong cluster group.
MessagingExamplesSelfTest#testMessagingPingPongExample should be unmuted on TC after merging the pull-request.
Check only Ignite Examples build on TC (there is no need to check all builds). All tests passed.

Upd. Actually, MessagingPingPongExample works fine.
The issue only about the unit-test, which run 2 nodes at the same jvm and localListen listen for both nodes, not only example node. The fix at the pull-request fix the test and doesn't broke the example.

It's need to fix java8 example too. Will do it at the same pull-request.

Last investigation results.

Then 2 nodes started at one jvm then
1. First send sends PING message to "remote" node
2. Remote listener send PONG message to "local" node here:

ignite.message(ignite.cluster().forNodeId(nodeId)).send(null, "PONG");

But as long as remote listener in the same jvm, then 

ignite.message(ignite.cluster().forNodeId(nodeId))

returns wrong IgniteMessaging instance for which locNodeId is nodeId of "local" node instead of nodeId of "remote" node. As a result, local listener gets wrong receiver node id.
